[spoiler=[b]Operation Red Falcon: Phase 3[/b]]
Hydronia had managed to capture most of the captured territory from both the zone 1 and zone 2 offensives. The Zone 2 offensive had crushed the ISV enclave, whilst the zone 1 attack had brought New Town and Al-Mosadr under Hydronian control. These cities would remain under Hydronian control for now, to ensure that the ISV could not launch a successful counteroffensive.

But, Hydronia wouldn't stop here. The final goal of this operation was to liberate vald and later all of the ISV's territory. To reach these goals however, Hydronian forces in the Zone 1 offensive would have to traverse the Dera Mountain Range, which tore through the middle of the country. It would take too much time and would be too costly too build a path across the harsh conditions of the mountains, which would further be intensified by the oncoming winter, so Hydronian troops would be forced to backtrack slightly to the city of Isles of Blueland. This city had been initially captured during the Hydronian landing operation, but later handed back over the Valdderan government forces in return for unobstructed use of it's transport links. Now, these links would be used.

The zone 1 offensive would be taken along the established blueland-pantheron highway across the Dera mountains, just on the outskirts of ISV territory. With close air support, the Hydronian troops would move swiftly towards Pantheron, marking one step closer to Vald. But, Hydronian forces couldn't progress to Vald just yet. In order to ensure that the capture of Vald would be a success, Hydronian forces would have to approach the city from all sides. So, the zone 1 army would progress along the highways to Adham Ronald and Later Fadh city.

This section of the offensive would take place deep within ISV territory, so Hydronian troops had to be careful. The airforce would first take out key targets in the area with it's HH-194Y multirole fighters (IRL F-16V). his would reduce resistance that ground troops would face. Once the ISVs positions had been suitably bombarded from above, ground troops would be permitted to roll in. The latest armoured technology from OtoHidro would protect the soldiers as they took enemy fire, whilst artillery would fire back twice as hard. The prior bombing of enemy artillery and other key targets would allow the Hydronians to hopefully overpower the ISV forces, allowing them to reach the settlement of Adham Ronald, before using the same tactics to reach and liberate Fadh city.

From this point, there would now only remain two major highways that lead into Vald that would not be under Hydronian control. Those highways connected Vald to Therene and Serene, two of Valdderas other major urban centres. A huge assault would be needed to liberate those cities, so Hydronia would begin airlifting more troops into Adham Ronald in preparation for Phase 4 of Operation Red Falcon.

Whilst complex logistics and tactics would be taking place in the Zone 1 offensive, the troops in Zone 2 would take a more brute approach to things. Whilst they had been capturing the ISV exclave, a wall of force had been built across the southern border of the ISVs eastern territory to protect the offensive from a northern counterattack. This wall would now come in very useful.

With no major highways or settlements in this part of the country, Hydronian troops would simply push hard to gain territory. The airforce would begin bombing operations across the entire eastern territory to decimate the ISVs defences across the frontline. Once the defences had been softened, Hydronia would be able to penetrate. Once again, armoured vehicles would roll across the Valdderan landscape, slowly gaining ground against the ISVs eastern stronghold.

Despite the easts lack of civilisation, it would come of great interest and importance to Hydronias special forces cobra team. Radio interceptions, cyber operations and intelligence reports would reveal that Hassan Al-Amin was residing somewhere within this territory. Equipped with this piece of information only, stealth helicopters would take off into the night with thermal sensors to slowly narrow down Hassans hiding place.

[i]You can run, but you cant hide[/i]
[/spoiler]
